'''Timothy Grant Leighton''' (born 16 October 1963)<ref name="whoswho"/><ref name=abubble/> is a British scientist. He is the Executive General Director and Inventor-in-Chief of [[Sloan Water Technology|Sloan Water Technology Ltd.]],<ref name="Sloan Water Technology Ltd. homepage">{{cite web|title=Sloan Water Technology Ltd. homepage|url= https://www.sloanwatertechnology.co.uk/ |access-date=2026-08-06}}</ref> best known for his work in bubble acoustics, planetary acoustics and medical acoustics. He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]], and Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref name=TripleCrown>{{cite web|title=TripleCrown |url=https://www.southampton.ac.uk/news/2018/05/tim-leighton-fellowship.page| year=2019}}</ref> He is emeritus professor of [[University of Southampton]], Honorary Professor of [[University College London]], and honorary fellow of Magdalene College at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="retires-2024">{{cite web|title= World-leading scientist and engineer Professor Timothy Leighton retires |url= https://www.southampton.ac.uk/engineering/news/2019/01/tim-leighton-doctor-of-science.page |access-date=2026-06-08}}</ref>

==Biography==
Leighton received a double first class Bachelor of Arts degree with honours in physics and [[theoretical physics]] from [[Cambridge University]] in 1985, and in 1988 he earned his PhD at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], University of Cambridge. Leighton was affiliated with the [[Institute of Sound and Vibration Research]], [[University of Southampton]], from 1992 to 2024 as a lecturer in [[underwater acoustics]] and was awarded a personal chair by University of Southampton at the age of 35. He founded and led two research organisations with international membership ([[#NAMRIP and Global-NAMRIP|Global-NAMRIP]] and [[#Health Effects of Ultrasound in Air|HEFUA]]).

==Public health==
===NAMRIP and Global-NAMRIP===
In 2015, Leighton founded the Global Network for AntiMicrobial Resistance and Infection Prevention (Global-NAMRIP).<ref name="NAMRIP_index">{{cite web|url=http://www.southampton.ac.uk/namrip/index.page?|title=NAMRIP homepage|publisher=The University of Southampton|access-date=2016-08-29}}</ref> Global-NAMRIP organised conferences, fostered collaborations and stimulated new areas of research, aimed at solutions that the end-users could implement for patients and public health. He is quoted as saying<ref>[https://www.southampton.ac.uk/namrip/publicengagment/oxford-talk-tim.page Maurice Lubbock Memorial Lecture at Oxford University]</ref> {{Blockquote|We need to work with rigour, imagination, and wonder, unconstrained by the artificial boundaries set in place by discipline names, or the history of projects in which we have previously worked, or the tendency of sponsors to believe they can pick winners, or above all by the belief that we must jump to solutions when we have not yet perceived the real problem. Then, when we eventually do find a solution, we must have the will to push it through all the way to help others, and not simply publish in the expectation that someone will finish the job for us.}}

===Health Effects of Ultrasound in Air===
In 2015, Leighton founded the research group Health Effects of Ultrasound in Air (HEFUA).<ref name="HEFUA_USRG">{{cite web|url=http://www.southampton.ac.uk/populationhealth/partners/HEFUA.page|title=HEFUA, Population Health, University of Southampton|publisher=The University of Southampton|access-date=2016-08-29}}</ref><ref name="HEFUA_project">{{cite web|url=http://www.southampton.ac.uk/engineering/research/projects/are-some-people-suffering.page|title=Ultrasound in Air, University of Southampton|publisher=The University of Southampton|access-date=2016-08-29}}</ref><ref name=hefua>{{cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/hefua2|title=HEFUA-2|website=sites.google.com|access-date=25 February 2015|archive-date=25 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150225172459/https://sites.google.com/site/hefua2/}}</ref> His aim was to map the increasing use of ultrasound in public places, and to investigate whether or not this increase is having adverse effects on some humans.
